help.howitworks.switching_service_source.backTranslation: Progress: when choosing a source would destroy progress already made, DebridPulse first asks Discard downloaded progress?. A service switch that would destroy progress is instead rejected, and the reason is given: Downloaded data would be discarded; switch its source to confirm.

While a download is paused: choosing another source for a file whose download had already started is accepted and saved, but nothing starts. The shown service and source stay the current ones, and a message next to the service name says where the file will go, for example Will switch to Real-Debrid (rapidgator.net) on resume. Choosing again changes it; choosing the source in use removes it. After resuming it shows Switching to … until the switch takes effect, then disappears. If a download's paused files will go to different places, or the destination is not known, no destination is shown. A file that never started has nothing to hand over, so its new source simply applies when it starts. Choosing a Service while paused works as described above, except that the download stays paused: a service that can take the link in use takes over immediately (the badge shows it), and one that must first prepare a copy shows Preparing … and takes over only after you resume. These messages appear on download activity and on the download rows; both kinds of messages can appear together.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.each_deb.backTranslation: Every debrid service has a Prepare backup torrents switch. It is on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox, whose torrent limits are stricter. When it is on, that service also adds torrents that another service is delivering, so that it is ready to take over the work if needed, and when you switch a download to another service, the torrent it had already started is kept as a backup instead of being removed. This uses that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first. Turn it off to keep that service's slots for its own downloads: its backups are then removed. An option you have already saved stays.

help.howitworks.backup_torrents.debrid_s.backTranslation: A debrid service can also add torrents that another service is delivering, so that it is ready to take over if needed, and when a download switches to another service, the torrent it had already started can be kept as a backup instead of being removed. This is each service's Prepare backup torrents setting: on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox; it is in that service's additional settings, which are part of the advanced presentation. Backups use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first.

A debrid service can also add torrents that another service is delivering, so that it is ready to take over the work if needed, and when a download is switched to another service, the torrent it had already started can be kept as a backup instead of being removed. This is each service's Prepare backup torrents setting: on by default for AllDebrid, Debrid-Link, Premiumize and Real-Debrid, and off by default for TorBox. Backups use that account's torrent slots and limits; a new download that needs a slot takes it back first.

help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.retry.backTranslation: Retry (or Reset) restarts a failed download from its original source, without adding it again. On a completed or removed download it downloads the files again.

help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.remov.backTranslation: Remove removes a download from the list. DebridPulse also cleans up the copy it created on the service and all incomplete partial files being written. Files that have been fully downloaded remain in your folder.

help.howitworks.pause_resume_retry.admin.backTranslation: An Administrator can remove, cancel or switch the source of any download. A User can do so only when no other account still needs that download, including downloads merged into it; otherwise the User withdraws their request in Requesters, and the download continues for everyone else.

help.howitworks.adding_same_thing.if_add.backTranslation: If you add a magnet, {file_type}, NZB or Metalink file that DebridPulse is already working on (including one that failed and has not been removed), it shows Already queued and keeps the existing download instead of starting a second one. Web links are always added as new downloads. Adding the same source again after a download has completed, been cancelled or been removed starts a new download. When it turns out that two downloads are fetching the same content, DebridPulse can merge them; the merged download shows Consolidated. When DebridPulse cannot prove that they match, the merged download instead shows Consolidated · Unverified. Merging does not change who requested it: each account's request remains its own.

help.settings.downloads.download_behavio.backTranslation: Download behavior and limits: Download folder (with Browse) and Maximum simultaneous downloads. Under Advanced settings: Content checkpoint interval and Graceful pause timeout (best left unchanged), Local network connections (off by default), which allows downloads from devices on your private network, and Skip local connection confirmation, which stops it asking every time. Even when allowed, DebridPulse never connects to the computer it runs on, nor to other non-private local addresses. Also there: Provider poll interval (how often the progress of work a service is preparing is checked), Full sync interval (how often downloads are reconciled with every enabled premium account that lists its transfers; 0 turns it off), and Retry on resolve failure with Delay before retry (minutes) (how many times and how soon a failed resolve attempt is tried again, for any service including network sources).

help.settings.users_access.user_accounts.backTranslation: User accounts lists every person with their role, how they sign in, and whether the account is enabled. Add local account creates an account with a username and password. A role changed in Edit user takes effect immediately: that person's open pages reload with the new role without signing them out. Every person has a DebridPulse username, which is separate from their display name: an OIDC account takes it from its first sign-in, and sign-in with a local password uses this name; the pencil next to it in the Edit user heading changes it and keeps any stored password. Click an account's name for its details and its activity, where a pending request can be withdrawn separately. Disable and Delete first show how many pending download requests the account has; those requests are withdrawn, a transfer that someone else also requested keeps running, and completed downloads are never touched. Disabling also ends the account's sign-in sessions and stops its tokens; deleting keeps the account's history and erases its own notification settings. When a deleted OIDC sign-in comes back, it gets a new account, which stays disabled until you enable it. Merge combines two or more accounts into the account you choose to keep; two accounts sharing the same verified email are pointed out, but only “Merge” combines them. help.settings.data_maintenance.backups.backTranslation: Backups opens the backup list. help.settings.data_maintenance.backups_r.backTranslation: Backups and retention: Scheduled backups in the Backup folder (on by default), whose Backup interval, Backup retention and Maximum backups to keep are under Additional backup and retention settings; a backup is removed when it becomes too old or is no longer among the newest backups you keep. help.topic.deployment_type.what_switchin.backTranslation: No account is deleted. Other people's accounts keep their username, password, identity provider links and saved enabled or disabled state. In Standalone they cannot sign in, whatever that state says.
It clears the built-in Administrator's password, turns off “Username and password” and OpenID Connect sign-in, and ends every browser session.
After this, sign-in is not required: anyone who can reach DebridPulse at an address it accepts can use it as the built-in administrator. This is not limited to this computer, and it does not expire.

help.topic.event_logging.principal_contr.backTranslation: “Recorded events” is the number of events currently kept. Events are kept indefinitely; only a database reset clears them.

findings.note: Reviewer: The trailing “जो “बैकअप फ़ोल्डर” में संग्रहीत होता है” could attach to the uploaded avatar rather than to the backup.
findings.resolution: Moved the relative clause next to बैकअप so it is the backup that is stored in the Backup Folder.

help.topic.backups.backups.while_enable.backTranslation: While “Enable” is on, a backup is made every “Backup interval”, and “Run backup” makes a backup now. “Backups” shows the list of stored backups, and lets you add, save, restore or delete a backup.

help.topic.backups.backups.backup.backTranslation: A backup is deleted when it becomes older than “Backup retention” or is no longer among the newest backups counted in “Maximum backups to keep”, whichever comes first.

help.topic.backups.backups.older_backups.backTranslation: Older backups are deleted according to the saved retention rules, which keep working; their settings are part of the Advanced presentation.

findings.note: Translator: Statistics Snapshot = आँकड़े स्नैपशॉट, matching settings.backups.snapshot_interval/keep_days.
findings.resolution: The translator chose the wording recorded in the note.

help.topic.backups.statistics_snapshots..backTranslation: Separately from this, DebridPulse saves a record of the last 24 hours of activity inside its own database every “Statistics snapshot interval”, and deletes snapshots older than “Statistics snapshot retention”. At 0, new snapshots stop being created.

help.topic.database_reset.intro.erases_d.backTranslation: Erases DebridPulse's download history, so that it starts empty. Use this only when you really want to start afresh.

help.topic.heading.what_removed_kept.backTranslation: What is removed and what remains

help.topic.database_reset.what_removed_k.backTranslation: Removed: records of transfers and their files, download requests, external jobs, events and activity logs, and statistics snapshots.
Remains: accounts, passwords, OpenID Connect links, API tokens, personal notification settings and every setting. Downloaded files on disk are not deleted.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.res.backTranslation: “Reset database” works only when “Allow database reset” is on, and it asks you for confirmation.

help.topic.database_reset.safeguards.pro.backTranslation: Processing pauses for the reset and afterwards returns to its previous state. A safety backup is made first; if it fails, nothing is deleted.

account.leave.message.backTranslation: Your unsaved changes in "My Account" will be lost.
